# Introduction

The programming courses use the Visual Studio Code (VSCode) IDE (Integrated Development Environment) to create programs in Python. VSCode is a versatile editor that supports extensions, allowing development in a wide range of languages. VSCode works across multiple platforms, making it a convenient tool for any developer. Best of all, it's free!

VSCode is a streamlined code editor with support for development operations like debugging, task running, version control, and much more. It aims to provide just the tools a developer needs for a quick code-build-debug cycle and leaves more complex workflows to [full featured IDE](https://code.visualstudio.com/) (@MicrosoftPythonVSCode2023).

:::{callout-note}
This document refer to the most current versions of Python, and VSCode as of this writing. Note that different computer setups and different versions means that the appearance of the screen shots in these documents may not match exactly your computer system.
:::

Follow these steps to install VSCode on your own computer. 

-   Install Python
-   Install VSCode
-   Install Python extension in VSCode
-   Getting Started with VS Code

This step-by-step tutorial will guide you through installing VSCode, a popular free code editor, along with the Python extension, which will make writing Python code a more productive experience.
